wy_wall_of_denial.blurb: Wall of Denial is a small sport crag in the lower part of Ten Sleep Canyon, reached by a short uphill walk of roughly ten minutes from the road. It holds 13 bolted routes, and the grades lean hard: a handful of 5.10s, one 5.11 and the majority in the 5.12 range, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. The wall stays shaded in the morning, which makes it a decent pick for a hot day or an early start. Debris from an old rockfall buried the base of a couple of lines, so expect awkward first clips on some routes. A cold chimney sits left of the main lines.

wy_warm_up_wall.blurb: Warm Up Wall is a sport crag on the Green Mile stretch of the Island Area near Cody. Despite the name, it is not especially easy: the 13 bolted routes are mostly 5.11, with a few 5.10s, one 5.9 and a single 5.12. Walls here look short but climb longer than they seem, with technical upper sections on small edges. Routes run to about 65 feet and finish on lower-off anchors, with around nine quickdraws needed on the longer ones. Best for climbers who are already comfortable on 5.10 and 5.11 and want a handful of quality lines in one spot.

wy_world_domination.blurb: World Domination is a large, clean sport face in the Mondo Beyondo zone of the upper Ten Sleep Canyon. All 13 routes are bolted and long, and the grades are demanding: one 5.10, two 5.11s and ten routes in the 5.12 range. The lines are sustained and slightly overhanging, so it rewards fit climbers with good endurance rather than those building up. A full 60 metre rope is likely needed to get back down safely. From the main parking lot, take the left-hand trail past the big boulder, head toward the Downpour wall, then follow the base of the cliff leftward.

wy_a_rising_from_the_plains.blurb: Rising From the Plains is a steep sport crag at the far west end of the Main Wall at Wild Iris, near Lander. A bulging low roof defines the left side, with a shorter wall of technical crimping to its right. Of its 12 routes, most fall between 5.12 and 5.13, with one 5.8, one 5.10 and one 5.11 mixed in, so it is a place for strong, powerful climbers. Lines are short, roughly 30 to 50 feet. It faces south and catches sun most of the day, though the right-hand routes shade over in the evening. It is the most exposed cliff at Wild Iris, and wind is a constant.

wy_4_far_right_warmup_area.blurb: Far Right is the fourth section of Hoback Shield, a limestone cliff in Hoback Canyon south of Jackson. It is the place to start: most of its 12 climbs are bolted routes in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, with one 5.11 and a couple of trad lines, plus a single boulder problem. The moderates are some of the best in the Jackson area, and the section is busy, so do not expect to be alone. The cliff as a whole faces south, which is pleasant in spring and fall but hot in summer once the sun reaches it. The trail climbs by switchbacks from the road, about ten minutes to the base.

wy_cheese_roof.blurb: Cheese Roof is a steep sport zone on the Dry Wall in the lower part of Ten Sleep Canyon, made up of bulges, columns and roofs just right of the Runaway Truck Ramp. It holds 12 bolted routes and is a hard-climber's area: a couple each of 5.10 and 5.11, two 5.12s, and the rest, six climbs, at 5.13 and 5.14. Expect powerful, sustained roof pulling rather than gentle warm-ups. The hardest lines here are among the most difficult at Dry Wall. Few moderate options exist, so it suits strong sport climbers.

wy_big_kahuna_pillar.blurb: Big Kahuna Pillar is a large, angular, free-standing pillar in the French Cattle Ranch zone of the upper Ten Sleep Canyon, just north of the Grasshopper Wall. It is reached by hiking past the Grasshopper Wall. The 12 routes are all bolted and sit in friendly territory for the canyon: two at 5.9, six at 5.10 and four at 5.11. That makes it a reasonable stop for climbers working through the middle grades, away from the hardest walls nearby. A few of the lines carry multiple stars from visitors.

wy_4_zeppelin_wall.blurb: Zeppelin Wall is the fourth section of Fairfield East, the rightmost crag on Fairfield Hill in Sinks Canyon near Lander. It is a sport wall of 12 routes, with technical, pocketed climbing on the 5.10 and 5.11 lines and a few 5.12s at the top end, plus one 5.8. The climbing here is mostly vertical to just under vertical. The section begins just past a giant slab leaning against the main cliff. Fairfield East overall has a gentle trail up from a two-track, one of the nicer walk-ins in Sinks, and many routes were rebolted and cleaned in 2019.
